preamble: The voiced velar plosive /g/ becomes the voiced alveolar sibilant [z] through palatalization and assibilation, usually via an affricate stage [dz]. In Slavic the second regressive palatalization turned *g before front vowels into *dz, which simplified to z everywhere except Polish and early Old Church Slavonic; in Venetan, Latin g before front vowels became [z]. A related outcome is the Indo-Iranian and Balto-Slavic (satem) treatment of the PIE palatovelar *ǵ, which gives Avestan and Slavic z.

examples.note: Second palatalization *g > *dz before the front vowel; Old Church Slavonic still writes кънѧѕь with the dz letter, while Russian and Czech kněz have z and Polish ksiądz keeps dz.
Satem reflex of the palatovelar; compare Sanskrit jñā- and Avestan zainti- 'understanding'.
Latin g before a front vowel gives [z], against Italian gente with [dʒ]; compare Istriot zento and Dalmatian ziant.
Iranian z continues the PIE palatovelar *ǵ; Middle Persian zand is from the same root.
